scope: Targeted candidate-text comparison only; not exhaustive novelty or literature evidence.

matches.hypothesis: W2 confidence may lack explicit readback of the FINAL predicted mask's pooled visual content into its language-conditioned query. Test whether a new mask-content aggregation path can supply task-relevant confidence evidence; upstream semantic attention already exists, and efficacy is not presumed.

Native query-language cross-attention computes a LayerNorm result but discards it before query self-attention. Its affine parameters therefore cannot learn language-conditioned query calibration. Reconnecting only the existing qla postnorm may remove residual common-mode/scale nuisance and restore a task-loss gradient path; this is a falsifiable implementation mechanism, not a promised accuracy improvement.

Masked language-padding feature values may leak through the native decoder into query confidence, although they represent no words. Test actual decoder attention/aggregation, not the semantic-alignment loss denominator addressed by historical Y23. If all native confidence paths mask these positions and matched interventions have no effect beyond repeat noise, reject THIS leakage premise without creating a model variant.

One output LayerNorm affine transform is reused for initial and six refined mask/score readouts although their query distributions differ. Independent per-stage affine readout normalization may reduce shared mask/score-gradient interference. This is an architectural allocation test; existing stage layers can implicitly compensate and benefit is unknown.

Native mask features x_mask(x) are expression-independent before their dot product with language-conditioned queries. A direct valid-language-conditioned channel modulation of the shared mask features may make conditional mask fitting easier. Existing query cross-attention can represent language interactions; this is an architectural comparison, not a missing-information, novelty or efficacy claim.

Native W2 averages coarse and fine visual query updates equally in all six refinement stages. A shared query-conditioned channel-wise bounded mixture may make the two spatial scales easier to combine. This changes representation fusion, not confidence targets or inference selection; neither missing information, novelty nor efficacy is presumed.

Native W2 adds projected sparse-3D and existing 2D appearance features before sum_norm. An explicit learned channel-product residual before that same normalization may ease visual interaction fitting. Existing downstream attention/MLPs may represent such interactions; neither missing information, novelty nor efficacy is presumed.

The original sampled query state is successively transformed by six contextual refinement stages. A shared zero-initialized residual from that same query slot original state may ease fitting a balance between initial anchor identity and later contextual updates. Existing residual paths already retain information; information loss, novelty and efficacy are not presumed.

The six existing query-language cross-attention outputs combine an incoming visual query with an attended-language update. A shared query-conditioned channel-wise gate on that existing update may ease fitting cross-modal updates. Native attention already depends on the query; no missing information, novelty or trained benefit is presumed.
